When there are k heads we flip coin k, so the head-count moves by exactly ±1 each step; the process terminates because it can be shown each configuration reaches all-tails.
Split configurations by the last coin. If coin n is T it is never flipped (it flips only at k=n) and the first n-1 coins run the ordinary (n-1)-process, contributing A_{n-1}.
If coin n is H, writing m=n-1, the first m coins run a shifted process (flip position j+1 given j heads) until all m are heads, then coin n flips, then the all-heads m-process takes m more steps.
This gives the recursion A_n = A_{n-1} + B_{n-1} + n·2^{n-1}, where B_m is the total of the shifted process over all 2^m configurations.
The averages A_n/2^n are 1/2, 3/2, 3, 5, i.e. twice them are 1, 3, 6, 10, the triangular numbers n(n+1)/2.
